figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1 | Discovery of a previously unknown halogenase. a, General  
rebound mechanism for C(sp3)–H functionalization in metalloenzymes. 
Mechanistically, M can be any metal that is able to activate C(sp3)–H bonds,  
and X can be an X-type ligand such as halides or pseudohalides coordinated to 
the metal centre. The copper-dependent halogenase, which belongs to the 
DUF3328 family, described in this work catalyses halogenation on unactivated 
C(sp3)–H bonds. αKG, α-ketoglutarate; HAA, hydrogen-atom abstraction.  
b, Proposed halide rebound mechanism of NHFeHal. c, Gene knockout  
study of apnU designated as the ΔapnU strain (based on P. oxalicum FO-125).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3 | Characterization of functional ApnU reveals a disulfide-bond-linked 
homodimer. a, Fast protein liquid chromatography (FPLC) chromatogram  
of refolded ApnU purified by AEX chromatography. Only peak I showed 
chlorination activity. b, Deconvoluted mass of the active fraction isolated from 
peak I in the AEX chromatogram. c, Predicted homodimer structure of ApnU  
by considering the experimentally determined disulfide bond pairings. The 
structure is shown as an AlphaFold2-predicted structure revised by Rosetta.
